shared_elements: frontal anthropomorphic figure on a vertical slab-shaped monument
elaborate headdress occupying the upper portion
low-relief carving covering the whole face of an upright stone
belt or waistband with pendant elements
serpent-like or fanged supernatural head motifs in the headgear
justification: Both depict a single frontal anthropomorphic personage carved in low relief across an upright slab, with a massive elaborate headdress at top incorporating zoomorphic/serpentine heads, a pectoral ornament at the chest and a belt with dangling elements below — a fairly specific shared scheme of one costumed figure filling the field. The chief difference is density and completeness: B is a crowded, detailed full-length standing figure with subsidiary heads, scrolls and a basal register, while A is a far more reduced, blocky composition dominated by a broad face/mask and simple discs with much of the lower body plain.
